newsitem.title: USA: Stryker says Q4 Japan sales off 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stryker says Q4 Japan sales off 20 pct.

text.p: Stryker Corp said sales in Japan declined 20 percent in the fourth quarter and 31 percent for the year due to lower shipments of products distributed by Matsumoto Medical Instruments Inc, a 51-percent owned unit, and unfavorable currency comparisons.
Sales of Matsumoto-distributed products, which are sourced by Matsumoto from other companies for sale in Japan, declined 49 percent in the fourth quarter and 58 percent for the year.
"The decline resulted from the termination of several distribution arrangements and unfavorable foreign currency comparisons in Japan," said Stryker, a medical devices maker.
Matsumoto posted a loss in the fourth quarter and the year, which reduced Stryker's operating income, effective income tax rate and minority interest charges, it said.

Stryker Monday said net sales for the fourth quarter ended December 31 were up nine percent over sales in the fourth quarter of 1995, while quarterly net earnings grew 20 percent and earnings per share grew 23 percent against a year ago.
For the year ended December 31, net sales increased four percent versus 1995, while net earnings were up 20 percent.

The company said domestic sales growth was 15 percent in the fourth quarter and 18 percent for the year on "strong shipments of endoscopic equipment, powered surgical instruments and orthopaedic implants and increased revenue from physical therapy services and higher shipments of hospital beds and stretchers."

The company said, "International sales were comparable to last year in the fourth quarter and declined 12 percent for the year as lower sales in Japan more than offset strong shipments in the other international markets."
It said, "Unfavorable currency comparisons, principally against the Japanese yen, reduced the dollar value of international sales by $6 million for the fourth quarter and $32.5 million for the year.
In addition, Stryker said several items were reflected in operating income in the fourth quarter of 1996, including:
--a $61.1 million gain on damages awarded and paid to Stryker for patent infringement, net of related attorney fees and expenses.
--a $41.8 million provision for special charges including write-downs.
--impairment in value of long-lived assets, reorganizations of distribution channels, settlement of patent infringement claims and purchased research and development expenses.

--a $13.8 million inventory adjustment, in excess of amounts recorded last year, for excess inventory and product deletions, principally in Japan, and obsolete inventory resulting from new product introductions.
